questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Decisive aspects for me were the country's culture and nature. I wanted to go on exchange somewhere that was far away from Denmark and different from both the culture/nature in Denmark, and so that you had the opportunity to experience and explore the other country and its culture.

How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: That's okay. Both UCPH and the host university send important emails that you should remember to read. They are also good at responding to emails from exchange students at Monash University.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a contact person, Rikki, who was good at answering emails and sending out attachments about orientation week, etc. So I felt like I had a lot of information when I came to Melbourne.

Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I would recommend that if you live off campus, get together with several people and find a place to live together. If possible, write to people you met at the information/orientation meeting from the University of Copenhagen who will be going to the same university as you. Start by renting yourself in an airbnb or hostel for the first few weeks, and then you could find accommodation on either "flatmates" or "fairy floss" on Facebook. Don't say yes to a place to live until you are in Melbourne and can actually evaluate the place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's a great opportunity to meet other people from all over the world and not only exchange students. Ended up living in a shared house with people from all over the world and it made the exchange special!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Just write with your contact person, if you have any questions.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The University of Copenhagen and the host university send out a lot of important emails, so be sure to read them through and check for deadlines.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Contact person from University of Copenhagen and Monash University were very helpful with different questions

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I luckily got all the courses, that I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you don't get all the courses you want to start with, it's possible you can still get them. I didn't get all the courses that I had as a first priority. But I ended up writing to the contact person from Monash University up until the start of my studies, where fortunately a spot became available in my desired class, which I was then put on. So if possible, write to the university continuously, as people often skip and cancel courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was okay. The level of some of the courses was a little lower than we might be used to at home, but still exciting courses to choose from.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very comparable, as there was both regular blackboard teaching and group work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Australian legal process and research - LAW5081
Indigenous peoples and the law - LAW5451
International criminal justice - LAW5354
Family violence, gender and law - LAW5469

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them, but I would especially recommend Family violence, gender and law, as the instructor was very committed and included guest speakers. Overall, a very good course with important social topics.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds like sports, law clubs, language clubs and more

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Board riders and language clubs to get to know other exchange students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore as much of Australia as possible! Make short get aways to Sydney, Brisbane, Perth. Do the Great Ocean Road and other stuff!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! The Aussies are so friendly and just very helpful!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just get to know people from the courses and join some clubs! Maybe see some footy games or rugby!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None that I can think of

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people! Very helpful and nice!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for a different academic culture, take advantage of the social and cultural opportunities and most importantly, plan your finances carefully

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over the world and experiencing Australia!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That it is an expensive country to live in - apply for all the grants/scholarships you can!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
